Selection barriers

Why a generic renovation portfolio cannot support every commercial project

A retail shop operating inside a mall, a vacant office and an occupied warehouse impose different constraints. AI must not mistake generic refurbishment for proven experience in all of them.

01

Live-business constraints are omitted

Night shifts, noise restrictions, permits to enter, mall management rules and tenant operations affect implementation. 'No disruption' is not credible without a site-specific plan.

02

Fit-out scope is confused with building services

Partitions, ceilings, electrical wiring, ventilation, fire-related equipment and commissioning may require distinct competencies. Contractor roles and subcontracting need to be stated accurately.

03

Completion deadlines lack site assumptions

Existing conditions, access, drawings, material lead times and sequencing determine timing. Promises to refurbish every shop within a set number of days are not defensible.

Verifiable facts

Evidence needed before a contractor appears in an AI shortlist

SP 71.13330.2017 remains the Russian code for specified insulation and finishing works, with Amendment 3 effective from 1 February 2026. Federal Law 384-FZ sets a building-safety framework within its scope. Citing either does not establish the contractor's compliance, project approvals or competence.

  • Actual project categories, contractor role, area, scope, permission to disclose photographs and timeline
  • Approved bills of quantities, stage schedule, building access rules, commissioning and handover
  • Relevant finishing and systems requirements, product records and substantiated subcontracting arrangements

This describes an evidence-led GEO method, not completed fit-out client results or measured improvement claims.

Scope of work

A commercial fit-out GEO process

I segment buyer questions by premises, access and real service scope, then verify information before publishing and testing recommendations.

  1. 01

    Record baseline AI recommendations

    Separate queries by offices, shops, food-service units and warehouses, work shifts, region and procurement profile.

  2. 02

    Verify past projects

    Check contractor scope, authorised case images, access conditions, estimates and claims about deadlines.

  3. 03

    Publish task-specific information

    Prepare briefs for site types, working arrangements, service boundaries and evidence-based case studies.

  4. 04

    Repeat AI tests

    Compare BMR and flag suggestions which overstate service capabilities or practical deadlines.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can a contractor guarantee uninterrupted office operations during fit-out?+

Not generically. Any phased plan and access/safety measures depend on the exact site and agreement with the client.

What is special about work in operating shopping centres?+

Management rules, working hours, material logistics and noise restrictions can differ from a vacant office. Only verifiable experience should be claimed.

Is SP 71.13330.2017 relevant in 2026?+

Rosstandart lists it as in force, and Amendment 3 became effective on 1 February 2026. Each provision's application must be assessed for the actual works.

Can a subcontractor's completed space be used as the company's own case?+

Only accurately, with its actual role and permitted images clearly described. Third-party delivery cannot be passed off as the contractor's own achievement.

What does commercial fit-out GEO cost?+

Published GAEO rates apply. Scope depends on premises types, served cities, genuine case evidence and the baseline prompt matrix.
